Number two is growling when you wake him up Pay close attention here, because this single misunderstanding sends good family dogs to shelters every week.

Number three is stealing your dirty socks from the laundry basket or hiding half-chewed treats and bones deep inside your bedsheets.
If you have ever walked out to the backyard in the morning and found one of your running shoes or a pair of socks sitting in the wet grass, you know how frustrating this gets.

Notice how your dog never steals clean folded towels out of the basket.
He always goes after the shirt you wore all day or the socks you just pulled off.
Your worn clothes hold a hundred times more of your scent than clean fabric.
When you leave the house holding your sock in his mouth is how an anxious or lonely dog keeps you close.

Wild canines bury food they cannot finish in the safest territory they can find, so scavengers do not steal it.
Because your bed holds the strongest concentration of your scent in the entire house, your dog's brain registers your mattress as a locked vault.
Just shake the sheets out and close your bedroom door when you leave, instead of scolding him for trusting your scent.
